_about: Lockheed L-1011 TriStar Maintenance Manual, 6-10-00 Figure 1, Aircraft Dimensions - Front and Side Views (page 2, Nov 15/78; EFFECTIVITY: ALL, the L-1011-1 airframe), page index 8 of 'Chapter 6.pdf' in the Internet Archive item chapter-22_202208: a scan of about 32 px a meter at this scale. layers.py --mode image --threshold 150 at scale 4, clip 70,130,530,345 (side). Pixels of that raster, line centres. The nose tip sits on the drawing's extension line (x 40): the nose's first meter is placed as free points. The windshield's front edge stands proud of the outline in this drawing (x 80-100): the crown is carried across its corner. The belly is hidden behind the nacelle (bridged). The S-duct's intake stands on the crown ahead of the fin, its lip 0.6 m above the crown on a short splitter: its top runs from the lip along the fairing's curve up into the fin's leading edge (the fin's root sits on it, where the leading edge's straight run begins), then is bridged under the fin to the rudder's foot and runs down the fairing to the tail cone; its bottom runs from the lip down the splitter to the crown and along it. The nozzle is the tail cone's last 2.1 m behind the cowl joint at x 1726.
